## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate cost-conscious deployment into concrete steps using Cloud Run, traffic management, and billing alerts. Covers practical, beginner-friendly use of core GCP DevOps tools without abstract theory.

## Key Concepts
- Cloud Run autoscaling knobs: concurrency, min/max instances
- Traffic splitting and revision management
- Cloud Billing budgets and alerts
- IAM basics for service, CI, and billing visibility

## Code Example
```bash
# Enable APIs
gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com

# Deploy v2 with autoscaling constraints
gcloud run deploy status-lookup-v2 \
  --image gcr.io/PROJECT/status-lookup:v2 \
  --region us-central1 \
  --platform managed \
  --concurrency 80 \
  --min-instances 0 \
  --max-instances 4

# Canary: 20% to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=20,status-lookup-v1=80

# 15 minutes later: 50/50
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=50,status-lookup-v1=50

# Final promotion: 100% to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic status-lookup --to-revisions status-lookup-v2=100

# Billing budget alert at $50/month
gcloud beta billing budgets create STATUS_LOOKUP_BUDGET --billing-account BLAHBLA --display-name "StatusLookup Budget" --amount 50 --thresholds 0.8 1.0
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate rollback if the alert triggers during a canary?
- What monitoring would you add to verify correct behavior across regions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical edge security using Google-native tooling and traffic filtering at the CDN/load balancer edge, a common requirement in regulated environments.

## Key Concepts
- Cloud Armor policy creation and rules
- Backend service association to a URL map
- Basic curl validation across allowed/blocked IPs
- Cloud Monitoring logs/alerts for denial events
- Minimal IAM bindings for security policies

## Code Example
```bash
# Create policy
gcloud compute security-policies create partner-ip-policy --description='Partner IP allow' --global

# Allow partner CIDRs
gcloud compute security-policies rules create 1000 --security-policy=partner-ip-policy --src-ip-ranges=192.0.2.0/24 --action=allow --direction=INGRESS
gcloud compute security-policies rules create 2000 --security-policy=partner-ip-policy --src-ip-ranges=198.51.100.0/24 --action=allow --direction=INGRESS

# Deny all other ingress
gcloud compute security-policies rules create 3000 --security-policy=partner-ip-policy --action=deny --direction=INGRESS

# Attach to backend
gcloud compute backend-services update-backend --global --backend-service=my-backend --security-policy=partner-ip-policy
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy changes in a staging environment?
- What are caveats when using Cloud Armor with dynamic backend instances?
